description: ERC-8262 provider protocol vectors. Fixtures only: no Oracle is deployed, every address, root and signer hash is illustrative, and wallets are PUBLIC Hardhat/Anvil TEST addresses. What each field means and what a conformant consumer reproduces: SPEC.md section 10.8. `limits` carries the protocol constants; `refusals` lists the refusals in check order.

schemaCases.name: discovery-native-two-sources
schemaCases.description: A native trust domain is one source.

schemaCases.name: discovery-single-label-trust-domain
schemaCases.description: trustDomainId is a DNS host with at least two labels.

schemaCases.name: discovery-attestor-zero
schemaCases.description: The Oracle rejects providerId 0.

schemaCases.name: discovery-attestor-not-decimal-string
schemaCases.description: attestorProviderId is a uint256 decimal string, never a JSON number.

schemaCases.name: discovery-key-without-material
schemaCases.description: A credential-root key names its credentialSigner.

schemaCases.name: discovery-carries-points
schemaCases.description: Scoring is the consumer's: no points, category or tier fields.

schemaCases.name: evidence-revoked-without-revoked-at
schemaCases.description: Revoked evidence states when.

schemaCases.name: evidence-active-with-revoked-at
schemaCases.description: revokedAt is present iff revoked.

schemaCases.name: evidence-checksummed-subject
schemaCases.description: Addresses are lowercase hex.

schemaCases.name: evidence-carries-points
schemaCases.description: Scoring is the consumer's: no points, category or tier fields.

schemaCases.name: evidence-credential-without-root
schemaCases.description: A proof type 4 artifact names its credential root.

schemaCases.name: evidence-claim-type-without-namespace
schemaCases.description: claimType is `<namespace>.<name>`.

schemaCases.name: evidence-guessable-id
schemaCases.description: evidenceId carries at least 128 bits (22 base64url characters).

schemaCases.name: evidence-id-trailing-newline
schemaCases.description: Patterns follow ECMA-262: no trailing line terminator before `$`.

schemaCases.name: discovery-zero-signer-hash
schemaCases.description: The all-zero hash marks an inactive signer slot; it is never a key's hash.

schemaCases.name: evidence-unknown-protocol-version
schemaCases.description: A consumer refuses a version it does not implement.

schemaCases.name: discovery-too-many-keys
schemaCases.description: At most 32 keys (likewise deployments, sources and claims per source).

schemaCases.name: discovery-unknown-protocol-version
schemaCases.description: A consumer refuses a version it does not implement.

schemaCases.name: discovery-ipv4-trust-domain
schemaCases.description: trustDomainId is never an IP literal (here the cloud metadata address).

schemaCases.name: discovery-numeric-last-label-trust-domain
schemaCases.description: A host whose last label is numeric is parsed as IPv4 by WHATWG URL (`0x7f.1` is 127.0.0.1): the last label starts with a letter.

schemaCases.name: discovery-updated-at-milliseconds
schemaCases.description: Timestamps are Unix seconds, at most 4294967295: a millisecond updatedAt fails the schema instead of locking the trust domain out.

schemaCases.name: discovery-attestor-above-uint256
schemaCases.description: attestorProviderId is at most 2^256 - 1.

schemaCases.name: discovery-revocation-check-too-short
schemaCases.description: revocationCheckSeconds is at least 60.

schemaCases.name: evidence-issued-at-beyond-uint32
schemaCases.description: Timestamps are at most 4294967295.

schemaCases.name: evidence-id-path-characters
schemaCases.description: evidenceId is base64url only: no `.`, `/` or `%` that a URL parser would rewrite.

evaluationCases.name: native-accepted
evaluationCases.description: Native trust domain, Base Sepolia, current key, root registered to attestor 7.

evaluationCases.name: gateway-accepted-base
evaluationCases.description: Gateway trust domain on Base: differs from native-accepted in source, trust domain, attestor, policy, expiry, chain and Oracle.

evaluationCases.name: gateway-human-tech-accepted
evaluationCases.description: One source behind the gateway.

evaluationCases.name: gateway-sumsub-accepted
evaluationCases.description: Another source behind the gateway: same trust domain and attestor. Its lifetime is exactly the 365-day maximum.

evaluationCases.name: gateway-signed-signals-accepted
evaluationCases.description: Proof type 7 claim; the current signed-signals key's hash is registered to attestor 1.

evaluationCases.name: alias-accepted-individually
evaluationCases.description: The consumer allowlists a second host of the gateway operator under the same attestor.

evaluationCases.name: rotation-retired-key-within-window
evaluationCases.description: Rotation, proof type 4: evidence issued by the retired credential-root key before its notAfter is not refused for the retirement; the Oracle still holds its root valid.

evaluationCases.name: replay-identical-redelivery
evaluationCases.description: Replay: the same evidenceId with identical fields is idempotent.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-id-scoped-by-trust-domain
evaluationCases.description: A recorded document of another trust domain that reuses this evidenceId and differs in every binding is no conflict: observations are keyed by (trustDomainId, evidenceId).

evaluationCases.name: discovery-newer-than-observed
evaluationCases.description: A document newer than the one observed earlier replaces it.

evaluationCases.name: issued-within-clock-skew
evaluationCases.description: issuedAt 60 seconds ahead of the consumer's clock is tolerated.

evaluationCases.name: impostor-host-not-allowed
evaluationCases.description: A host outside the consumer's allowlist copying the gateway's attestor, root key and root: its documents alone would pass every later check.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-not-from-discovery-host
evaluationCases.description: Evidence obtained anywhere but the trust domain's own host (a push body, a relay, another provider) is unauthenticated.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-unavailable
evaluationCases.description: The discovery fetch failed (here 503). A consumer never substitutes a cached copy for a fetch.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-gone
evaluationCases.description: 410 Gone for the announced evidenceId is final: the consumer records (trustDomainId, evidenceId) as revoked.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-not-found-is-fetch-failure
evaluationCases.description: 404 is a fetch failure, not revoked: refused at step 7 for now and never recorded, so a provider misdeploy is recoverable.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-redirect-is-fetch-failure
evaluationCases.description: A consumer never follows redirects: a 3xx is a fetch failure (step 7).

evaluationCases.name: discovery-names-other-trust-domain
evaluationCases.description: An allowlisted host serving a document that names another trust domain.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-from-other-trust-domain
evaluationCases.description: Native evidence presented under the gateway's discovery document.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-duplicate-deployment
evaluationCases.description: Two attestors for one deployment in one document: one trust domain would count twice in a quorum.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-duplicate-key
evaluationCases.description: A keyId listed twice (here once revoked): first-match and last-match consumers would disagree.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-duplicate-source
evaluationCases.description: A sourceId listed twice.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-rolled-back
evaluationCases.description: A document older than one the consumer observed (a stale cache or rollback).

evaluationCases.name: replay-across-chains
evaluationCases.description: Base evidence presented to a Base Sepolia consumer.

evaluationCases.name: replay-across-oracles
evaluationCases.description: Right chain, different Oracle deployment.

evaluationCases.name: attestor-not-declared
evaluationCases.description: Native evidence claiming attestor 1 while the consumer pins the native trust domain to attestor 7.

evaluationCases.name: impostor-pinned-to-other-attestor
evaluationCases.description: The consumer onboarded the host as attestor 9; its documents claim attestor 1. The pin, not the document, decides.

evaluationCases.name: claim-type-not-declared
evaluationCases.description: human-tech declares personhood.unique only.

evaluationCases.name: policy-not-declared
evaluationCases.description: A policyId the source does not declare.

evaluationCases.name: claim-declared-by-another-source
evaluationCases.description: persona evidence naming a (claimType, policyId, proofType) that only sumsub declares: claims are declared per sourceId, never per trust domain.

evaluationCases.name: key-not-declared
evaluationCases.description: keyId absent from discovery.

evaluationCases.name: key-use-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 4 artifact naming a signed-signals key.

evaluationCases.name: rotation-revoked-key
evaluationCases.description: Key revocation is retroactive: issuedAt inside the key's window does not help.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-not-reversible
evaluationCases.description: A newer document that drops a key's revokedAt does not restore the key: the consumer remembers revocations per trust domain.

evaluationCases.name: rotation-retired-key-after-window
evaluationCases.description: Rotation: the retired key cannot issue after its notAfter.

evaluationCases.name: rotation-retired-signals-key
evaluationCases.description: Rotation, proof types 7-9: a retired signed-signals key ends at notAfter, even for evidence issued inside its window and even while the Oracle still holds its hash.

evaluationCases.name: credential-signer-not-on-oracle
evaluationCases.description: The current credential-root key's credentialSigner is not the Oracle's getCredentialSigner for the attestor.

evaluationCases.name: revocation-root-revoked-on-oracle
evaluationCases.description: Revocation on-chain: the root is no longer valid for attestor 1.

evaluationCases.name: revocation-signer-hash-revoked-on-oracle
evaluationCases.description: Revocation on-chain: the signed-signals hash was revoked from the registry.

evaluationCases.name: replay-across-wallets
evaluationCases.description: Evidence for one wallet presented for another.

evaluationCases.name: replay-evidence-id-reused
evaluationCases.description: Same evidenceId, different immutable field (an in-place extension).

evaluationCases.name: revocation-status-revoked
evaluationCases.description: The provider reports the evidence revoked.

evaluationCases.name: revocation-not-reversible
evaluationCases.description: An active response after the consumer recorded the revoked body of revocation-status-revoked.

evaluationCases.name: validity-window-empty
evaluationCases.description: expiresAt equal to issuedAt.

evaluationCases.name: validity-too-long
evaluationCases.description: expiresAt one second past the 365-day maximum lifetime.

evaluationCases.name: issued-in-future
evaluationCases.description: issuedAt 61 seconds ahead of the consumer's clock.

evaluationCases.name: expired
evaluationCases.description: expiresAt is exclusive: now == expiresAt is expired.

evaluationCases.name: proof-multi-signed-slots-include-key
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof whose active signer slots include the evidence key's hash, next to another provider's slot, matches.

evaluationCases.name: proof-attestor-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: A verified proof type 4 proof for the same wallet whose provider_id is another attestor (the gateway's): it does not feed this evidence.

evaluationCases.name: proof-provider-mismatch-same-root
evaluationCases.description: provider_id differs while credential_root is the evidence's: only the provider_id input is wrong.

evaluationCases.name: proof-root-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: provider_id matches, but credential_root is another root the attestor holds valid.

evaluationCases.name: proof-credential-type-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: The proof attests another credential type than the evidence names.

evaluationCases.name: proof-submitter-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: The proof was submitted by another wallet than the evidence's subject: the Oracle recorded it for that wallet, so provenance (the record's subject) refuses it.

evaluationCases.name: proof-type-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: The evidence feeds proof type 4; the verified proof is a type 9 proof signed by the same trust domain's signed-signals key.

evaluationCases.name: proof-signer-hash-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 7 proof signed by another attestor's registered key does not feed evidence naming the gateway's key.

evaluationCases.name: proof-multi-signed-slots-omit-key
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof whose two active signer slots (attestors 1 and 12) do not include the evidence key.

evaluationCases.name: proof-signer-hash-of-sibling-key
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 7 proof signed by another key of the same trust domain (the retired gw-signals-0, whose hash the Oracle still holds) does not feed evidence naming gw-signals-1.

evaluationCases.name: proof-multi-signed-slot-of-sibling-key
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof whose only gateway slot is the sibling gw-signals-0 does not feed evidence naming gw-signals-1.

evaluationCases.name: registry-holds-only-sibling-key
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle holds the hash of another key of the trust domain (gw-signals-0) but not of gw-signals-1, the key the evidence names.

evaluationCases.name: risk-score-signed-accepted
evaluationCases.description: Proof type 8 (RISK_SCORE_SIGNED) evidence fed to a matching type 8 proof.

evaluationCases.name: risk-score-signed-hash-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: A type 8 proof signed by the sibling key gw-signals-0.

evaluationCases.name: statement-signed-other-accepted-jurisdiction
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 7 proof under US rules, the second jurisdiction the consumer accepts, feeds the evidence.

evaluationCases.name: statement-signed-jurisdiction-not-accepted
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 7 proof signed by the evidence key under a jurisdiction the consumer does not accept (UAE): the wallet chose a more lenient risk threshold, and the Oracle verified it.

evaluationCases.name: statement-signed-config-differs
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 7 proof under another registered weight configuration (config_hash) than the consumer requires.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-direction-differs
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 8 proof of "score > 3000" where the consumer requires "score < 3000": signed by the evidence key and verified by the Oracle, it proves the opposite.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-bound-differs
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 8 proof of "score < 10000", which any score below the maximum meets and the Oracle accepts as non-trivial.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-range-not-threshold
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 8 range proof (score in [0, 3000], the SDK's direction 0) where the consumer requires the threshold proof score < 3000.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-config-differs
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 8 proof under another weight configuration (config_hash).

evaluationCases.name: statement-multi-signed-jurisdiction-not-accepted
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof under a jurisdiction the consumer does not accept (UAE).

evaluationCases.name: statement-multi-signed-config-differs
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof under another weight configuration (config_hash).

evaluationCases.name: statement-multi-signed-threshold-below-floor
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof with threshold_m 1 where the consumer requires at least 2 signers, although two slots are active.

evaluationCases.name: statement-multi-signed-threshold-above-floor
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof with threshold_m 3 over three attestors' slots meets a floor of 2.

evaluationCases.name: statement-missing-signed
evaluationCases.description: A consumer with no statement for proof type 7 refuses the evidence, though its proof matches: it cannot tell what the proof must prove.

evaluationCases.name: statement-missing-risk
evaluationCases.description: As statement-missing-signed, for proof type 8.

evaluationCases.name: statement-missing-multi-signed
evaluationCases.description: As statement-missing-signed, for proof type 9.

evaluationCases.name: statement-for-other-type
evaluationCases.description: The consumer's statement is for proof type 9 (at least two signers) and the evidence is proof type 7. The type 7 proof's jurisdiction and config_hash meet the statement's, but a statement for another proof type is no statement for this evidence.

evaluationCases.name: statement-on-credential-evidence
evaluationCases.description: The consumer requires a proof type 7 statement and is given proof type 4 evidence, whose matching proof proves only its credentialType.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-threshold-free-upper
evaluationCases.description: A threshold proof (score < 3000) whose bound_upper is 5000 rather than the SDK's 0: risk_score_signed leaves bound_upper free in threshold mode, so it proves the statement and is accepted.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-range-accepted
evaluationCases.description: A range proof (score in [1000, 3000]) in the SDK's encoding (direction 0) proves a range statement.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-range-free-direction
evaluationCases.description: The same range proof with direction 2: risk_score_signed leaves direction free in range mode, so it is accepted.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-range-proof-type-differs
evaluationCases.description: A threshold proof (score < 1000, bound_upper 3000 left free) for a range statement [1000, 3000]: every bound word matches, only proof_type differs.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-range-upper-differs
evaluationCases.description: A range proof [1000, 5000] for a range statement [1000, 3000]: only bound_upper differs.

evaluationCases.name: statement-risk-range-lower-differs
evaluationCases.description: A range proof [500, 3000] for a range statement [1000, 3000]: only bound_lower differs.

evaluationCases.name: provenance-inputs-not-verified-signed
evaluationCases.description: The wallet presents proof type 7 inputs under EU rules, but the Oracle verified the same proof's inputs under UAE rules: keccak256 of the presented words is not the attestation's publicInputsHash.

evaluationCases.name: provenance-inputs-not-verified-credential
evaluationCases.description: The presented proof type 4 inputs name the evidence's root; the Oracle verified a proof against the attestor's older root.

evaluationCases.name: provenance-attestation-subject-differs
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle's attestation was recorded for another wallet than the evidence's subject, whatever the presented submitter input says.

evaluationCases.name: provenance-attestation-proof-type-differs
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle's attestation records proof type 8 for inputs presented as a proof type 7 proof.

evaluationCases.name: proof-submitter-mismatch-signed
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 7 proof signed by the evidence key for another wallet. The Oracle records a proof for its submitter, so the record's subject is that wallet and provenance refuses it before the submitter word is read (the two cannot disagree on-chain, SPEC.md section 10.5).

evaluationCases.name: proof-submitter-mismatch-risk
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 8 proof signed by the evidence key for another wallet: refused by provenance (the record's subject), as proof-submitter-mismatch-signed.

evaluationCases.name: proof-submitter-mismatch-multi-signed
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof carrying the evidence key's slot, for another wallet: refused by provenance (the record's subject), as proof-submitter-mismatch-signed.

evaluationCases.name: signals-hash-registered-to-other-attestor
evaluationCases.description: The gateway lists gw-signals-2 with the native attestor's public signer hash: the Oracle registers that hash to attestor 7, not the pinned 1, so one signature cannot feed two attestors' evidence.

evaluationCases.name: registry-lacks-attestor-signed
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle holds no registration for attestor 1 at all: proof type 7 evidence is refused, never waved through.

evaluationCases.name: registry-lacks-attestor-risk
evaluationCases.description: The same for proof type 8 evidence.

evaluationCases.name: registry-lacks-attestor-multi-signed
evaluationCases.description: The same for proof type 9 evidence.

evaluationCases.name: proof-stale-signed-attestation-revoked
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle reports a proof type 7 attestation revoked.

evaluationCases.name: proof-stale-risk-attestation-expired
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 8 attestation that expired one second ago.

evaluationCases.name: proof-stale-multi-signed-before-issuance
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof timestamped 61 s before the evidence was issued.

evaluationCases.name: proof-attestation-expires-now
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle attestation is live through its expiresAt (block.timestamp <= expiresAt): now == expiresAt still feeds.

evaluationCases.name: proof-attestation-expired
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle attestation expired one second ago: a held grant does not outlive it.

evaluationCases.name: proof-attestation-revoked
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle reports the attestation revoked (isAttestationRevoked: guardian-invalidated or verified by a revoked verifier version).

evaluationCases.name: proof-timestamp-within-skew-of-issuance
evaluationCases.description: A proof timestamp 60 s before issuedAt is tolerated (prover and provider clocks).

evaluationCases.name: proof-timestamp-before-issuance
evaluationCases.description: A proof made 61 s before the evidence was issued (e.g. under an earlier, since-revoked evidence) does not feed it.

evaluationCases.name: proof-timestamp-at-evidence-expiry
evaluationCases.description: expiresAt is exclusive for the proof timestamp too.

evaluationCases.name: order-proof-mismatch-before-stale
evaluationCases.description: A proof of another attestor (proof_mismatch) whose attestation has also expired (proof_stale).

evaluationCases.name: evidence-id-dot-segments
evaluationCases.description: An announced evidenceId with dot segments would leave /v1/erc8262/evidence/ once a URL parser normalizes it; it fails the evidenceId rule and is never fetched.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-id-percent-encoded
evaluationCases.description: Percent-encoded dot segments are refused the same way: `%` is outside the rule.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-id-trailing-newline
evaluationCases.description: Patterns follow ECMA-262: `$` does not match before a trailing line terminator, so an id ending in a newline fails the rule (a Python re.search-style check would let it through).

evaluationCases.name: evidence-id-too-short
evaluationCases.description: An announced evidenceId shorter than 22 characters carries under 128 bits.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-id-body-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: The host answers the request for one evidenceId with another valid document of its own.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-id-case-differs
evaluationCases.description: evidenceIds compare exactly: a body whose id differs only in case is another id.

evaluationCases.name: key-material-relisted-under-new-id
evaluationCases.description: After gw-root-0 was revoked, a newer document drops it and lists its credentialSigner as gw-root-2 (and the attestor re-points the Oracle to it): revocation is remembered by key material, not only keyId.

evaluationCases.name: key-material-relisted-in-same-document
evaluationCases.description: One document lists gw-root-0 as revoked and its credentialSigner again as gw-root-2: the revoked material is refused under the new keyId with no earlier document.

evaluationCases.name: key-revoked-at-future-instant
evaluationCases.description: A revokedAt after the consumer's clock still revokes: revocation is the field's presence, never its value.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-two-oracles-one-chain
evaluationCases.description: Two deployments on one chainId with different Oracle addresses are distinct, not duplicates.

evaluationCases.name: revocation-attestor-denied-on-oracle
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle guardian denied attestor 7 (isProviderDenied): its evidence is refused although its root is still registered and the Oracle's ATTESTATION path does not check denial itself.

evaluationCases.name: revocation-attestor-denied-signed
evaluationCases.description: A denied attestor's proof type 7 evidence is refused although its signer hash is still registered.

evaluationCases.name: latest-block-attestor-denied
evaluationCases.description: denyProvider(7) is included but not yet finalized: the finalized reads still show attestor 7 allowed, the latest block shows it denied. A refusal at either block refuses (a held grant is suspended).

evaluationCases.name: finalized-block-attestor-denied-lifted-at-latest
evaluationCases.description: undenyProvider(7) is included but not yet finalized: the latest block shows attestor 7 allowed, the finalized reads still show it denied. Acceptance rests on the finalized reads, so it is refused.

evaluationCases.name: latest-block-root-revoked
evaluationCases.description: revokeCredentialRoot on the evidence's root is included but not yet finalized: refused at step 23 from the latest block.

evaluationCases.name: finalized-block-root-not-yet-registered
evaluationCases.description: The evidence's root is registered at the latest block but not yet at the finalized one: acceptance rests on the finalized reads, so it is refused at step 23.

evaluationCases.name: latest-block-signer-hash-revoked
evaluationCases.description: revokeSignerPubkeyHash on the key's signer hash is included but not yet finalized: a proof type 7 evidence is refused at step 23 from the latest block.

evaluationCases.name: latest-block-config-revoked
evaluationCases.description: revokeConfig on the config_hash the statement names is included but not yet finalized: refused at step 23 from the latest block.

evaluationCases.name: latest-block-attestation-revoked
evaluationCases.description: invalidateAttestation on the proof is included but not yet finalized: refused at step 31 from the latest block. A held grant is suspended, not ended, until the revocation is read at the finalized block (a reorganization can still drop it).

evaluationCases.name: latest-block-credential-signer-not-read
evaluationCases.description: A setCredentialSigner for attestor 7 is included but not yet finalized. Step 22 compares a rotation, not a revocation, and reads only at the finalized block, which still holds the key's credentialSigner: accepted. (The Oracle switches the signer as soon as the call is included; an emergency switch reaches step 22 only once finalized, SPEC.md section 10.5.)

evaluationCases.name: attestation-revoked-at-both-blocks-ends
evaluationCases.description: invalidateAttestation on the proof is finalized: the attestation reads revoked at both blocks. A step-31 revocation read at the finalized block ends a held grant, whatever the latest block also reads.

evaluationCases.name: attestation-expired-latest-reads-differ-ends
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle attestation expired a second ago while the latest block's reads differ from the finalized ones on something else (attestor 12 denied at the latest block). The expiry is a finalized-block step-31 cause, so a held grant ends: only an attestation revocation read at the latest block alone suspends.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-finalized-equals-latest-accepted
evaluationCases.description: The finalized tag resolves to the latest block itself, same number and timestamp: a chain with instant finality, or an anvil node with fewer than 64 blocks (anvil answers finalized as its head minus 64 blocks, floored at 0). Equal is not after, so the pair is usable.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-equal-timestamps-accepted
evaluationCases.description: The finalized block is 64 blocks behind the latest one with the same timestamp (anvil_mine mines a batch of blocks in one second): equal timestamps are not out of order, so the pair is usable.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-other-chain
evaluationCases.description: The node answers for Base (chain 8453) while the consumer's deployment is on Base Sepolia, where the Oracle could sit at the same address: the pair is invalid, so the evaluation is unavailable and suspends a held grant.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-invalid-before-stale
evaluationCases.description: The node answers for Base and its latest block is also older than the age bound: the validity checks come first, so blocks_invalid, not blocks_stale.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-finalized-after-latest
evaluationCases.description: The finalized tag resolves to a higher number than the latest tag: no node on one chain answers that, so the pair is invalid.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-finalized-timestamp-after-latest
evaluationCases.description: The numbers are in order but the finalized block's timestamp is after the latest block's: the pair is invalid.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-from-the-future
evaluationCases.description: The latest block's timestamp is 61 s after the consumer's clock (a fabricated or mis-parsed head, or a node on another network): the pair is invalid and never read.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-timestamp-within-skew-accepted
evaluationCases.description: The latest block's timestamp is exactly 60 s after the consumer's clock: within the skew, so the pair is usable and the evaluation completes.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-stale
evaluationCases.description: The latest block is 121 s old by the consumer's clock (a stuck node, or a load-balanced RPC answering from a lagging replica): its latest-block revocation and denial reads would miss anything included since, so the pair is stale. The evaluation reads no Oracle state and is unavailable: it grants nothing, and a held grant's re-evaluation cannot complete, so the grant is suspended until one accepts.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-age-at-bound-accepted
evaluationCases.description: The latest block is exactly 120 s old: at the bound is not older than it, so the pair is usable.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-stale-read-never-refuses
evaluationCases.description: On a stale pair the latest block still shows attestor 7 denied (undenyProvider was included since). A stale pair is not read at all: no refusal at step 21, but unavailable, which suspends a held grant all the same.

evaluationCases.name: block-pair-invalid-expired-still-ends
evaluationCases.description: As expired, on a pair from another chain: invalid like stale, so steps 24-29 still run and the expiry ends a held grant.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-suspended-by-latest-denial
evaluationCases.description: denyProvider(7) is included at the latest block: the exercised grant's re-evaluation is refused at step 21 and suspends it (a denial can be lifted, so it does not end the grant).

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-lifted-by-accepting-re-evaluation
evaluationCases.description: After held-grant-suspended-by-latest-denial, undenyProvider(7) is included (or the block that carried the denial is reorganized away). The re-evaluation accepts, which lifts the suspension: the grant's next re-evaluation is due at now + the smaller of the trust domain's revocationCheckSeconds (3600) and the consumer's deployment maximum (1800). A replica lagging inside the staleness bound that has not yet seen the denial lifts it the same way (SPEC.md section 10.9, Residuals).

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-suspended-by-fetch-failure
evaluationCases.description: After held-grant-lifted-by-accepting-re-evaluation, the discovery fetch fails (503): a fetch failure refuses at step 6, records nothing, and suspends the grant until a re-evaluation accepts.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-recheck-capped-by-consumer
evaluationCases.description: A consumer lowers its deployment maximum to 600, below even the gateway's revocationCheckSeconds (900), while its grant's recheckBy (now + 1800) was recorded under the earlier maximum (1800). It re-evaluates the grant at once, as lowering requires, and the accepting re-evaluation sets the next re-evaluation due at now + 600, earlier than the recorded one. A provider can lower the interval, never raise it past the consumer's maximum.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-shortened-recheck-carried
evaluationCases.description: After held-grant-recheck-capped-by-consumer, the store holds the shorter recheckBy (now + 600) that re-evaluation wrote, not the later one recorded before it: a recheckBy is overwritten by each accepting re-evaluation, never kept as the later of the two.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-suspended-on-stale-pair
evaluationCases.description: An exercised grant, its next re-evaluation not due for 15 minutes, is re-evaluated on a node whose latest block is 121 s old. The re-evaluation cannot complete, so it suspends the grant (recheckBy null) however long its recorded recheckBy still runs: an unusable pair never keeps a grant, not even until its recheckBy.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-lifted-after-stale-pair
evaluationCases.description: After held-grant-suspended-on-stale-pair, the store holds the grant suspended (recheckBy null), not its earlier recheckBy. A re-evaluation on a usable pair accepts and lifts the suspension: due at now + 1800.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-suspended-on-other-chain-pair
evaluationCases.description: After held-grant-lifted-after-stale-pair, the grant's next re-evaluation is not due until now + 1800, and it is re-evaluated through a node answering for Base (chain 8453) instead of Base Sepolia: the pair is invalid, so the re-evaluation suspends the grant (recheckBy null) however long its recheckBy still runs.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-lifted-after-other-chain-pair
evaluationCases.description: After held-grant-suspended-on-other-chain-pair, the store holds the grant suspended; a re-evaluation through a node on the deployment's chain accepts and lifts it.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-of-other-subject-untouched
evaluationCases.description: As replay-across-wallets: another wallet announces the subject's evidenceId (any party holding the bearer id can), and the evaluation is refused at step 24. The store holds the subject's own grant on that evidence, host and proof: a grant is keyed by the subject too, so the refusal suspends only the announcing wallet's grant on it, if one existed, never the subject's.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-of-subject-kept-after-other-wallet
evaluationCases.description: After held-grant-of-other-subject-untouched, the subject's grant is still exercised with its recheckBy unchanged, and its own re-evaluation accepts. A store keying grants by host and evidenceId alone suspends it at the other wallet's refusal.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-on-old-proof-ends-alone
evaluationCases.description: The subject holds two grants on one evidence from one host: one on an older proof whose Oracle attestation expired one second ago, one on a newer proof of the same evidence made an hour ago (a renewal: a new evaluation, so a new grant). Re-evaluating the old proof is refused at step 31, which ends the old proof's grant only: a grant is keyed by the proof hash too.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-on-renewed-proof-kept
evaluationCases.description: After held-grant-on-old-proof-ends-alone, the renewed proof's grant is still held with its recheckBy unchanged, and its own re-evaluation accepts. A store keying grants without the proof hash ends it with the old proof's.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-ended-under-its-own-host-only
evaluationCases.description: The subject holds two grants on one evidenceId and proof: one from the native host, one from the gateway (the subject knows the id, and any allowlisted host can serve it). The gateway answers 410 for it: the gateway's grant ends and the revocation is recorded under the gateway. A grant is keyed by the fetch host and the announced id (with the subject and the proof hash), so the native host's grant is untouched.

evaluationCases.name: held-grant-of-other-host-kept
evaluationCases.description: After held-grant-ended-under-its-own-host-only, the native host's grant on the same evidenceId is re-evaluated: the gateway's 410 is recorded under the gateway, so it is accepted and kept. A store keying grants or revocations by evidenceId alone ends or refuses it.

evaluationCases.name: revocation-gone-not-reversible
evaluationCases.description: A 410 recorded earlier for this (trustDomainId, evidenceId) is final: a later 200 with status active is refused.

evaluationCases.name: gone-scoped-by-trust-domain
evaluationCases.description: A 410 recorded for the same evidenceId under another trust domain does not affect it.

evaluationCases.name: revocation-scoped-by-evidence-id
evaluationCases.description: A revocation recorded for another evidenceId of the same trust domain does not affect this one: a revocation never spreads to the host's other evidence.

evaluationCases.name: revoked-body-names-other-trust-domain
evaluationCases.description: The allowlisted gateway serves a schema-valid revoked body naming the native trust domain and carrying the native evidence's id, which it was announced: refused at step 5 and recorded under the gateway host, never under the trustDomainId the body names.

evaluationCases.name: revocation-from-other-host-not-applied
evaluationCases.description: The native evidence of that id is still accepted from its own host: the revocation the gateway caused is keyed by the gateway host.

evaluationCases.name: recorded-revocation-looked-up-by-fetch-host
evaluationCases.description: The native host's revocation of an id is recorded; the gateway serves an active body naming the native trust domain under that id. Step 5 looks up (gateway host, announced id), finds nothing, and the body is refused for naming another trust domain.

evaluationCases.name: recorded-revocation-looked-up-by-announced-id
evaluationCases.description: A revocation is recorded for (gateway host, announced id); the host answers with an active body carrying another of its ids. Step 5 looks up the announced id, so it refuses before the body's id is compared.

evaluationCases.name: gone-from-host-not-allowed
evaluationCases.description: A 410 from a host outside the allowlist: refused at step 1 and never recorded.

evaluationCases.name: gone-for-invalid-announced-id
evaluationCases.description: A 410 for an announced id that fails the evidenceId rule (a consumer never fetches it; a 410 changes nothing): refused at step 2 and never recorded.

evaluationCases.name: recorded-revocation-evidence-not-found
evaluationCases.description: A revocation is recorded and the evidence fetch now answers 404: the recorded revocation refuses (step 5), not the fetch failure (step 7).

evaluationCases.name: recorded-revocation-evidence-unavailable
evaluationCases.description: The same with the evidence fetch answering 503.

evaluationCases.name: recorded-revocation-evidence-timeout
evaluationCases.description: The same with no HTTP response to the evidence fetch (a timeout).

evaluationCases.name: key-id-relisted-with-new-material
evaluationCases.description: After gw-root-0 was revoked, a newer document lists the keyId gw-root-0 again with fresh key material and no revokedAt: revocation is remembered by keyId as well as by material.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-rolled-back-one-second
evaluationCases.description: A document one second older than the one recorded is stale: staleness compares instants of the provider's one clock, with no skew.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-two-oracles-two-attestors
evaluationCases.description: Two Oracles on one chain with different attestors (9 on the other Oracle, listed first): step 14 reads the deployment of the evidence's (chainId, oracleAddress), never the first of its chainId.

evaluationCases.name: signals-rotation-overlap-successor
evaluationCases.description: During a signed-signals rotation overlap, evidence issued under the successor (whose hash the Oracle holds next to the predecessor's) is accepted while the predecessor still serves.

evaluationCases.name: signals-rotation-overlap-predecessor
evaluationCases.description: In the same overlap the predecessor's evidence is still accepted: it ends at the predecessor's notAfter.

evaluationCases.name: signals-rotation-overlap-predecessor-issued-in-overlap
evaluationCases.description: Evidence the predecessor gw-signals-1 issued inside the overlap (after the successor's notBefore, before its own notAfter) is accepted: both keys issue until the predecessor's notAfter.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-shared-by-alias-host
evaluationCases.description: The consumer recorded the gateway's document revoking gw-root-1. The alias host, pinned to the same attestor, still lists that credentialSigner as current: the revocation applies to it by key material.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-not-shared-across-attestors
evaluationCases.description: The consumer recorded a gateway document that lists the native attestor's public signer hash as its own revoked gw-signals-2. The native trust domain is pinned to another attestor, so the gateway cannot revoke its key: accepted.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-shared-after-recorder-unlisted
evaluationCases.description: The consumer recorded the gateway's document revoking gw-root-1 under attestor 1, then removed the gateway from its allowlist. The revocation stays recorded under the attestor pinned when it was recorded, so it still applies to the alias host pinned to attestor 1.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-shared-to-any-domain-pinned-to-attestor
evaluationCases.description: The consumer recorded the gateway's revocation of gw-root-1 under attestor 1 and pins a further host, the impostor, to attestor 1; its document names attestor 1 and lists the same credentialSigner as current. A recorded key revocation applies to every trust domain pinned to its attestor now. The store holds no pin history, so this case reads the same whether the host was pinned before or after the recording: SPEC.md section 10.7 makes the rule time-free, and this vector holds only that it reaches a host other than the operator's own alias.

evaluationCases.name: gateway-re-pinned-accepted
evaluationCases.description: The consumer re-pinned the gateway to attestor 5, which now holds the gateway's credential signer and root; its newer document names 5 and lists gw-root-1 as current. With no key revocation recorded, the gateway's evidence under attestor 5 is accepted.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-kept-by-recorder-after-re-pin
evaluationCases.description: As gateway-re-pinned-accepted, but the consumer recorded the gateway's earlier document revoking gw-root-1 while it pinned the gateway to attestor 1. A trust domain's own key revocation applies to it whatever attestor it is pinned to now: re-pinning never forgets it, and the newer document that lists gw-root-1 without revokedAt does not restore it.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-not-recorded-under-disputed-pin
evaluationCases.description: The consumer mis-pins the gateway to attestor 7 (the native host's). The gateway's document names attestor 1 and lists the native host's signer hash as its own revoked gw-signals-2. The evaluation is refused at attestor_mismatch; the document is still recorded, but its key revocations are recorded under no attestor (attestorProviderId null), because the document does not name the pin: a mis-pinned host never revokes the pinned attestor's material.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-of-mis-pinned-host-not-shared
evaluationCases.description: The store holds what key-revocation-not-recorded-under-disputed-pin recorded, and the gateway is still pinned to attestor 7. The native host, pinned to 7, lists that signer hash as its current nk-signals-1: a revocation recorded under no attestor applies to its own trust domain alone, so the native evidence is accepted.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-colliding-key-id-not-shared
evaluationCases.description: The consumer recorded the alias host's document revoking its own key gw-signals-1, whose material differs from the gateway's gw-signals-1. Across trust domains a revocation matches key material only, never a keyId: the gateway's evidence under its gw-signals-1 is accepted.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-under-none-not-reversible
evaluationCases.description: As key-revocation-not-reversible, but the consumer recorded the gateway's document revoking gw-root-0 while it mis-pinned the gateway to attestor 7, so under no attestor (null). The pin is since corrected to 1. A revocation recorded under none still applies to its own trust domain, whatever it is pinned to: the newer document that drops gw-root-0's revokedAt does not restore it.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-under-none-by-key-id
evaluationCases.description: As key-id-relisted-with-new-material, with gw-root-0's revocation recorded under no attestor (a mis-pin since corrected). For its own trust domain a revocation recorded under none applies by keyId as well as by material: the keyId relisted with fresh material is refused.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-under-none-by-material
evaluationCases.description: As key-material-relisted-under-new-id, with gw-root-0's revocation recorded under no attestor (a mis-pin since corrected). For its own trust domain a revocation recorded under none applies by material as well as by keyId: the material relisted as gw-root-2 is refused.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-recorded-under-none-while-mis-pinned
evaluationCases.description: The consumer mis-pins the gateway to attestor 7. The gateway's document names attestor 1 and revokes gw-root-1: refused at attestor_mismatch, and the document is recorded with its revoked keys under no attestor (null).

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-under-none-not-shared-with-alias
evaluationCases.description: The store holds what key-revocation-recorded-under-none-while-mis-pinned recorded, and the gateway is still mis-pinned. The alias host, pinned to attestor 1, lists gw-root-1's credentialSigner as current: a revocation recorded under none reaches no other trust domain, so the alias evidence is accepted.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-re-recorded-after-pin-corrected
evaluationCases.description: The store holds what key-revocation-recorded-under-none-while-mis-pinned recorded; the consumer then corrects the gateway's pin to attestor 1 and fetches the same document again. It revokes gw-root-1, so the evidence is refused at key_revoked, and the document's revoked keys are now recorded under attestor 1, beside the record under none: a key revocation record is keyed by (trustDomainId, recording attestor or none, keyId, material), so the one under none never stops this insert.

evaluationCases.name: key-revocation-shared-after-pin-corrected
evaluationCases.description: The store holds both records of gw-root-1's revocation: under none (written while mis-pinned) and under attestor 1 (key-revocation-re-recorded-after-pin-corrected). The one under attestor 1 is shared: the alias host, pinned to 1 and listing that credentialSigner as current, is refused. A store that let the record under none block the later one would accept here.

evaluationCases.name: config-revoked-on-oracle-signed
evaluationCases.description: The guardian revoked the config_hash the consumer's statement names (isValidConfig false): a proof type 7 evidence is refused at step 23 even though its proof verified before the revocation.

evaluationCases.name: config-revoked-on-oracle-risk
evaluationCases.description: As config-revoked-on-oracle-signed, for proof type 8.

evaluationCases.name: config-revoked-on-oracle-multi-signed
evaluationCases.description: As config-revoked-on-oracle-signed, for proof type 9.

evaluationCases.name: config-not-read-for-credential
evaluationCases.description: Proof type 4 carries no config_hash: an Oracle holding no config valid does not refuse it.

evaluationCases.name: config-of-statement-for-other-type-not-read
evaluationCases.description: The consumer's statement is for proof type 7 and names a config_hash the Oracle no longer holds valid; the evidence is proof type 8. Step 23 reads only the statement for the evidence's proof type, so this evidence is refused at step 30 (a statement for another type), not at step 23.

evaluationCases.name: proof-multi-signed-key-in-last-slot
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 9 proof with all five signer slots active carries the evidence key's hash in the last one (input 10, signer_pubkey_hash_4).

evaluationCases.name: recorded-revocation-refetched-revoked
evaluationCases.description: The store already holds the revocation revocation-status-revoked recorded, and the host serves the revoked body again: refused, and the insert-if-absent revocation write still counts.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-body-fails-schema
evaluationCases.description: A 200 whose discovery body fails its schema (here a points field) is a fetch failure: refused at step 6, never recorded.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-unsupported-protocol-version
evaluationCases.description: A discovery document of a protocolVersion the consumer does not implement.

evaluationCases.name: evidence-unsupported-protocol-version
evaluationCases.description: An evidence body of a protocolVersion the consumer does not implement is a fetch failure (step 7), never revoked.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-updated-at-within-skew
evaluationCases.description: A discovery updatedAt 60 seconds ahead of the consumer's clock is tolerated.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-updated-at-in-future
evaluationCases.description: A discovery updatedAt 61 seconds ahead (one past the skew) is refused and not recorded, so it cannot make every later document stale.

evaluationCases.name: root-registered-to-other-attestor
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle holds the root valid, but registered to attestor 7, not the gateway's attestor 1.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-attestor-differs-from-pin
evaluationCases.description: The evidence names the pinned attestor 7, but the discovery document names 9 for the deployment.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-lacks-deployment
evaluationCases.description: The discovery document does not list the evidence's deployment.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-same-updated-at
evaluationCases.description: Re-fetching the document already recorded (equal updatedAt) is not stale.

evaluationCases.name: discovery-stale-per-trust-domain
evaluationCases.description: A newer document recorded for another trust domain does not make this one stale: staleness compares only documents of the same trust domain.

evaluationCases.name: issued-at-key-not-before
evaluationCases.description: issuedAt equal to the key's notBefore is inside its window.

evaluationCases.name: issued-before-key-not-before
evaluationCases.description: issuedAt one second before the key's notBefore.

evaluationCases.name: issued-last-second-before-key-not-after
evaluationCases.description: issuedAt one second before the retired key's notAfter is inside its window.

evaluationCases.name: issued-at-key-not-after
evaluationCases.description: notAfter is exclusive: issuedAt equal to it is outside the window.

evaluationCases.name: signals-key-retired-at-not-after
evaluationCases.description: A signed-signals key is retired from the instant the consumer's clock equals notAfter.

evaluationCases.name: signals-key-last-second-before-not-after
evaluationCases.description: One second before notAfter the signed-signals key still serves.

evaluationCases.name: deployment-mismatch-chain-only
evaluationCases.description: The consumer's Oracle address, another chain.

evaluationCases.name: proof-type-not-declared
evaluationCases.description: human-tech declares personhood.unique for proof type 4 only, not 7.

evaluationCases.name: credential-signer-checked-before-announced-not-after
evaluationCases.description: nk-root-2026b carries a future notAfter: 61 s before it the key is still current, so its credentialSigner must be the Oracle's (here the Oracle holds another).

evaluationCases.name: credential-signer-not-checked-within-skew-of-not-after
evaluationCases.description: From 60 s before notAfter the key is no longer current: a consumer whose clock lags the provider's by up to the skew does not compare against an Oracle that already holds the successor.

evaluationCases.name: order-not-allowed-before-evidence-id
evaluationCases.description: Host outside the allowlist (trust_domain_not_allowed) and an invalid announced evidenceId (evidence_id_invalid).

evaluationCases.name: order-evidence-id-before-origin
evaluationCases.description: Invalid announced evidenceId (evidence_id_invalid) and evidence from another host (origin_mismatch).

evaluationCases.name: order-origin-before-gone
evaluationCases.description: A 410 relayed from another host (origin_mismatch before evidence_gone): only the discovery host's own 410 is recorded.

evaluationCases.name: order-gone-before-discovery-unavailable
evaluationCases.description: A 410 from the allowlisted host while its discovery fetch fails (evidence_gone before discovery_unavailable): the revocation is final and recorded even during a discovery outage.

evaluationCases.name: order-gone-before-discovery-invalid-body
evaluationCases.description: A 410 from the allowlisted host while its discovery body fails the schema (evidence_gone before discovery_unavailable).

evaluationCases.name: gone-during-outage-stays-revoked
evaluationCases.description: The 410 recorded during the discovery outage is final: discovery is back and the host answers 200 active, refused (evidence_revoked).

evaluationCases.name: revoked-body-during-discovery-outage
evaluationCases.description: A schema-valid revoked body for the announced id from the allowlisted host while its discovery fetch fails: refused and recorded as revoked under (host, evidenceId). Only status and evidenceId are read.

evaluationCases.name: revoked-body-recorded-refuses-during-outage
evaluationCases.description: The revocation recorded from the revoked body refuses the next fetch (200 active) before the discovery checks, while the discovery fetch still fails.

evaluationCases.name: revoked-body-with-invalid-discovery
evaluationCases.description: A revoked body while the host's discovery body fails its schema: refused and recorded as revoked.

evaluationCases.name: revoked-body-id-mismatch-during-outage
evaluationCases.description: A revoked body for another evidenceId than the announced one during a discovery outage is not recorded; the outage is the refusal.

evaluationCases.name: revoked-body-id-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: The same id-mismatched revoked body with discovery available: not recorded.

evaluationCases.name: revoked-body-fails-schema-during-outage
evaluationCases.description: A revoked body that fails the evidence schema (no revokedAt) during a discovery outage is not recorded; the outage is the refusal.

evaluationCases.name: revoked-body-fails-schema
evaluationCases.description: The same schema-invalid revoked body with discovery available: a fetch failure (step 7), not recorded.

evaluationCases.name: revoked-body-from-relay
evaluationCases.description: A revoked body fetched from another host than discovery's (a relay): origin_mismatch, not recorded.

evaluationCases.name: order-gone-before-revoked
evaluationCases.description: A 410 (evidence_gone) for an id already recorded as revoked (evidence_revoked).

evaluationCases.name: order-discovery-unavailable-before-evidence-unavailable
evaluationCases.description: Both fetches fail, discovery with 503 and evidence with 404 (discovery_unavailable before evidence_unavailable).

evaluationCases.name: order-evidence-unavailable-before-trust-domain
evaluationCases.description: A 404 for the evidence (evidence_unavailable) and a discovery document naming another trust domain (trust_domain_mismatch).

evaluationCases.name: order-trust-domain-before-evidence-id-mismatch
evaluationCases.description: Evidence of another trust domain (trust_domain_mismatch) whose id is not the one requested (evidence_id_mismatch).

evaluationCases.name: order-evidence-id-mismatch-before-discovery-invalid
evaluationCases.description: A body for another evidenceId (evidence_id_mismatch) under a document repeating a keyId (discovery_invalid).

evaluationCases.name: order-discovery-invalid-before-future
evaluationCases.description: A document repeating a keyId (discovery_invalid) whose updatedAt is more than the skew ahead of the clock (discovery_from_future).

evaluationCases.name: order-future-before-stale
evaluationCases.description: A document ahead of the clock (discovery_from_future) that is also older than one recorded (discovery_stale).

evaluationCases.name: order-stale-before-deployment
evaluationCases.description: A stale document (discovery_stale) and evidence for another deployment (deployment_mismatch).

evaluationCases.name: order-deployment-before-attestor
evaluationCases.description: Another Oracle (deployment_mismatch) and an attestor other than the pin (attestor_mismatch).

evaluationCases.name: order-attestor-before-claim
evaluationCases.description: The consumer pins the gateway to attestor 9 (attestor_mismatch) and the claim is undeclared (claim_not_declared).

evaluationCases.name: order-claim-before-key
evaluationCases.description: An undeclared policyId (claim_not_declared) and an undeclared keyId (key_not_declared).

evaluationCases.name: order-key-use-before-revoked
evaluationCases.description: A proof type 7 claim naming a credential-root key (key_use_mismatch) that is revoked (key_revoked).

evaluationCases.name: order-revoked-before-window
evaluationCases.description: A revoked key (key_revoked) named by evidence issued after its notAfter (key_not_valid_at_issuance).

evaluationCases.name: order-window-before-retired
evaluationCases.description: A signed-signals key named by evidence issued after its notAfter (key_not_valid_at_issuance), and retired at evaluation (key_retired).

evaluationCases.name: order-retired-before-denied
evaluationCases.description: A retired signed-signals key (key_retired) of an attestor the Oracle has denied (attestor_denied).

evaluationCases.name: order-denied-before-credential-signer
evaluationCases.description: A denied attestor (attestor_denied) whose Oracle credential signer also differs from the current key's (credential_signer_mismatch).

evaluationCases.name: order-credential-signer-before-registry
evaluationCases.description: The Oracle holds another credential signer (credential_signer_mismatch) and no longer holds the root (not_registered_on_oracle).

evaluationCases.name: order-registry-before-subject
evaluationCases.description: A root no longer on the Oracle (not_registered_on_oracle) presented for another wallet (subject_mismatch).

evaluationCases.name: order-subject-before-conflict
evaluationCases.description: Another wallet (subject_mismatch) and an evidenceId reused with a changed field (evidence_id_conflict).

quorumCases.name: gateway-two-sources-one-trust-domain
quorumCases.description: Two KYC sources (persona, sumsub) re-signed by one gateway: one trust domain, one attestor, so 2-of-N is NOT met.

quorumCases.name: native-and-gateway-two-trust-domains
quorumCases.description: One native and one gateway trust domain: two attestors, quorum met.

quorumCases.name: three-sources-two-trust-domains
quorumCases.description: Three KYC sources across two trust domains count two.

quorumCases.name: alias-host-shares-attestor
quorumCases.description: Two allowlisted hosts pinned to one Oracle providerId are one trust domain on-chain and count once.

quorumCases.name: refused-member-not-counted
quorumCases.description: Only evidence that passes the section 10.5 evaluation counts.

quorumCases.name: impostor-not-counted
quorumCases.description: A host outside the allowlist claiming the gateway's attestor adds nothing.

quorumCases.name: claim-types-not-pooled
quorumCases.description: A personhood claim does not count toward a KYC requirement.

quorumCases.name: multi-signed-two-trust-domains
quorumCases.description: Proof type 9 KYC from the native and the gateway trust domains: two attestors, quorum met.

quorumCases.name: proof-types-not-pooled
quorumCases.description: A proof type 4 credential does not count toward a proof type 9 requirement.

quorumCases.name: attestors-sorted-numerically
quorumCases.description: attestors lists providerIds in ascending numeric order: 7 before 12, though `12` sorts first as a string.

quorumCases.name: observed-revocation-not-counted
quorumCases.description: Members are evaluated against the consumer's observation store: a 410 it recorded for the gateway evidence removes that member.

quorumCases.name: proof-mismatched-member-not-counted
quorumCases.description: The native trust domain's type 4 proof (provider_id 7) presented for the gateway evidence does not feed it, so it counts only for the native attestor. A proof counts for an attestor only when it feeds that attestor's evidence (a type 9 proof whose slots carry both keys feeds both, see multi-signed-two-trust-domains).

quorumCases.name: stale-member-not-counted
quorumCases.description: The gateway member's proof matches its evidence, but the Oracle reports that attestation revoked: step 31 runs for every member, so it does not count.

quorumCases.name: statement-mismatched-member-not-counted
quorumCases.description: The gateway member's proof type 9 proof carries its key's slot but was made under UAE rules, which the requirement's statement does not accept: it does not count.

quorumCases.name: multi-signed-no-statement-counts-none
quorumCases.description: A proof type 9 requirement with no statement: every member is refused at step 30 (a consumer with no statement for 7, 8 or 9 refuses), so nothing counts.

quorumCases.name: key-revocation-shared-across-members
quorumCases.description: Two gateway members fetched different copies of the gateway's discovery document: one revokes gw-root-1, the other does not. The revoked key that one member's evaluation records applies to every member before counting, so the gateway does not count on that key.

quorumCases.name: evidence-revocation-shared-across-members
quorumCases.description: The gateway evidence is announced twice: one fetch answers 410, the other the active body. The revocation the 410 member records applies to every member before counting, so the active copy does not count.

quorumCases.name: key-revocation-not-shared-across-attestors-in-quorum
quorumCases.description: The gateway member's discovery document lists the native attestor's public signer hash as its own revoked gw-signals-2. Shared revocations keep their keying: a key revocation reaches a member of another trust domain only when that one is pinned to the attestor it was recorded under, so the native member still counts.

quorumCases.name: key-revocation-of-mis-pinned-member-not-shared
quorumCases.description: The consumer mis-pins the gateway to attestor 7, the native host's. The gateway member is refused at attestor_mismatch (its document and evidence name attestor 1), and the revoked gw-signals-2 its document lists, the native host's signer hash, is recorded under no attestor because the document does not name the pin. It applies to the gateway alone, so the native member still counts.

quorumCases.name: latest-block-denial-in-quorum
quorumCases.description: denyProvider(1) is included but not yet finalized: the quorum's one latest block shows the gateway's attestor denied. Steps 21, 23 and 31 read both blocks for every member, so the gateway member is refused and does not count.

quorumCases.name: latest-block-root-revoked-in-quorum
quorumCases.description: revokeCredentialRoot on the native evidence's root is included but not yet finalized: refused at step 23 from the quorum's latest block, so the native member does not count.

quorumCases.name: quorum-block-pair-stale
quorumCases.description: The quorum resolves one block pair when it starts and checks it once every member's fetches have completed, before any Oracle read: its latest block is then 121 s old. The whole quorum is unavailable and counts no member, while each member still runs the steps that read no block and records what they record: the gateway's 410 is recorded as revoked, and the native member's document as any evaluation's.

quorumCases.name: quorum-block-pair-invalid
quorumCases.description: The quorum's node answers for another chain: its one block pair is invalid, so the quorum is unavailable and counts no member.
